title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

The group began by reading the following accounts without adding explanations of its own. The theory explains how several observations fit into a larger pattern. Without measurements, her explanation remained a conjecture rather than a fact. The meaning of the ancient symbol remains an enigma to historians. One idiosyncrasy of the teacher was her habit of singing the date aloud.

It then considered a second group of accounts, looking for both similarities and differences. The photograph of a dragon proved to be a clever hoax. The museum records the fishing lore passed down through coastal families. The orchestra played a medley of tunes from several musicals. The old insult grew into a bitter vendetta between the two families.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

something mysterious or difficult to understand
